source_name: BBC by Lana Lam, syndicated by AOL
summary:
Australia's online safety regulator has reported gaps in the ways four gaming platforms protect children. The report examined Steam, Roblox, Fortnite and Minecraft.

Online games are popular with young people. Research cited by the BBC says nine out of ten Australian children aged eight to seventeen have played them. That makes the design of safety systems an important public issue.

The regulator compared how companies identify harmful material, check ages and share safety information. It found that their approaches were not consistent. Some services generally let people state their own age, which is different from checking whether that age is correct.

The report used company information covering October 2025 through March 2026. That timing matters: a report about earlier systems may not describe every change made later.

Roblox told the BBC that protecting users is a priority and that it has invested in safeguards. The BBC also asked the other companies for comment.

The report calls attention to the responsibilities of the companies that run gaming spaces. It asks how those spaces can better protect the children who use them.
title: Australia Reviews Safety on Online Game Platforms
why_it_matters: Many young people use online games, making the quality of platform safeguards important.
